verdict: Kroger's sales rose 2% to $34.6B and profit grew to $641M as eCommerce sales jumped 20%, but identical sales without fuel barely grew — up just 0.2% — and Kroger trimmed its full-year sales outlook.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: total sales vs a year ago

kpis.label: Identical sales
kpis.note: without fuel, vs +3.4% a year ago

segments.name: Supermarket sales (ex-fuel)
segments.note: Sales to retail customers without fuel — groceries, pharmacy and general merchandise, in stores and online. Down 0.5% as Inflation Reduction Act changes cut pharmacy reimbursement rates, even though identical sales without fuel rose 0.2%.

segments.name: Supermarket fuel sales
segments.note: Gasoline sold at supermarket fuel centers — up 26% on higher fuel prices and volumes. Fuel carries a much lower margin than groceries.

segments.name: Other sales
segments.note: Wholesale and other sales outside the supermarkets.

opex.name: Operating, general & administrative
opex.note: Store labor and the cost of running the business day to day — Kroger's OG&A line, 17.2% of sales.

opex.name: Rent
opex.note: Rent on leased stores and facilities.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Wear-and-tear cost of stores, warehouses and technology, spread over their useful lives.

otherDetail: Net other expense of $132M on this chart: interest expense, net of $156M and $9M of non-service pension cost, partly offset by a $34M gain on investments — plus $1M of earnings attributable to noncontrolling interests, so the bottom line is the $641M attributable to Kroger.
follow100Note: A supermarket keeps very little of each sales dollar: about $1.86 of every $100 became profit this quarter. Merchandise — the food and goods on the shelves — took $77.30.

takeaways.title: Underlying sales barely grew
takeaways.text: Identical sales without fuel rose just 0.2%, including a roughly 1.4-point headwind from the Inflation Reduction Act's effect on pharmacy sales. Kroger cut its full-year identical-sales guidance to 0.2%–0.8%.

takeaways.title: Digital is the growth engine
takeaways.text: Adjusted eCommerce sales grew 20% and Kroger Precision Marketing profit grew 24%, with eCommerce profitability improving — a bright spot that helped offset higher shrink and transportation costs in stores.

takeaways.title: Adjusted EPS rose 5%
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS was $1.05. Excluding adjustment items, EPS was $1.09, up 5%, and adjusted FIFO operating profit was $1,076M versus $971M on a GAAP basis — the gap is mainly the $39M LIFO charge plus transformation and litigation items.

oneTimers: Adjustment items excluded from adjusted EPS netted to +$26M after tax: $43M of transformation costs and $9M of merger-related litigation charges, partly offset by a $26M after-tax adjustment removing investment gains. Adjusted net earnings were $667M ($1.09 per share) versus $641M ($1.05) GAAP.
Merchandise costs include a $39M LIFO charge — an accounting cost that rises when the cost of goods inflates — down from last year, which helped the gross margin rate.
footerNote: Kroger's fiscal second quarter ended August 15, 2026. Kroger reports a single operating segment; the sales split shown (retail sales without fuel, fuel, other) is the breakdown in its Q2 2026 Form 10-Q. Gross profit here is sales less merchandise costs (including warehousing, transportation and the $39M LIFO charge), exactly as Kroger's statement of operations foots; Kroger's own quoted gross margin rate of 22.4% uses a slightly different definition. Net income is the $641M attributable to Kroger (consolidated net earnings were $642M).
